newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK watchdog investigating 175 securities cases.
newsitem.headline: HK watchdog investigating 175 securities cases.

text.p: Hong Kong's financial markets watchdog is investigating a total of 175 cases of possible misconduct, which include insider dealing and market manipulation, Mark Dickens, executive director of the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) said on Thursday.
"A lot of listed companies are not pro-active in giving out information," Dickens told a news conference.
When misconduct is suspected, the SFC needs to try to intervene earlier than it is doing at present, before damage is done, he said.
The commission also needs to streamline its operation to improve efficiency, he said.
He said the SFC had adequate powers and he expects no major changes in the rules over the next few years.
Hong Kong had compared its enforcement record with those in other Asian Pacific countries, including Japan, Australia and New Zealand, and believed its was superior, Dickens said,
There are "organised people" behind market manipulation activities, Dickens said, but added they are "not always one group" and "not always the same group".
